items.question: Which is correct? 'I enjoy ___ in the sea.'
items.explanation: <Enjoy> siempre va seguido del gerundio (-ing): enjoy swimming.

items.question: After prepositions (in, at, of, about), we use:
items.explanation: Tras preposición el verbo va en -ing: good at cooking, interested in learning.

items.question: Which group of verbs takes the gerund (-ing)?
items.explanation: <Avoid/mind/suggest> piden -ing; <want/hope/decide> piden infinitivo con to.

items.question: Escribe UNA palabra: 'She decided ___ study medicine.'
items.explanation: <Decide> pide infinitivo con <to>: decided to study.

items.question: "I am happy," she said. → She said she ___ happy.
items.explanation: En estilo indirecto el presente retrocede a pasado: am → was.

items.question: "I have seen that film," he said. → He said he ___ that film.
items.explanation: El present perfect retrocede a past perfect: have seen → had seen.

items.question: "Don't run!" → He told the children ___ run.
items.explanation: Órdenes negativas en indirecto: told + objeto + not to + infinitivo.

items.question: Escribe UNA palabra: '"I will call you," he said.' → He said he ___ call me.
items.explanation: <Will> retrocede a <would> en estilo indirecto.

items.question: You're coming tonight, ___?
items.explanation: La coletilla invierte el auxiliar del verbo principal: are → aren't you.

items.question: Let's have lunch, ___?
items.explanation: Tras <Let's> la coletilla es siempre <shall we>.

items.question: She hardly ever complains, ___?
items.explanation: <Hardly ever> es negativo, así que la coletilla va en positivo.

items.question: Complete: 'If it ___ tomorrow, we will cancel the picnic.'
items.explanation: Primer condicional: If + presente simple, will + infinitivo.

items.question: Complete: 'If I had a car, I ___ you to the airport.'
items.explanation: Segundo condicional: If + pasado simple, would + infinitivo.

items.question: Escribe UNA palabra: 'I won't go ___ you come with me.' (= only if)
items.explanation: <Unless> equivale a <if... not>: no iré a menos que vengas.

items.question: Complete: 'She ___ to Peru three times.'
items.explanation: <Has been> = fue y volvió; <has gone> implica que sigue allí.

items.question: Complete: 'I ___ here since 2019.'
items.explanation: Con <since> + momento se usa present perfect.

items.question: Complete: 'While I ___ dinner, the phone rang.'
items.explanation: Acción larga interrumpida: past continuous + past simple.

items.question: Escribe UNA palabra: 'I have known her ___ ten years.'
items.explanation: <For> mide duración; <since> marca el punto de inicio.

items.question: Complete: 'You ___ wear a seatbelt — it's the law.'
items.explanation: <Must> expresa obligación fuerte, típicamente legal.

items.question: Complete: 'You ___ pay — the museum is free today.'
items.explanation: <Don't have to> = no es necesario; <mustn't> = está prohibido.

items.question: Complete: 'When I was six I ___ swim quite well.'
items.explanation: <Could> expresa habilidad general en el pasado.

items.question: Complete: 'This exercise is ___ than the last one.'
items.explanation: Adjetivos largos: more + adjetivo + than.

items.question: Complete: 'It's the ___ film I have ever seen.'
items.explanation: Superlativo irregular de <bad>: bad – worse – worst.

items.question: Escribe UNA palabra: 'She isn't ___ tall as her brother.'
items.explanation: Comparación de igualdad: as + adjetivo + as.

items.question: What is a <round-trip ticket>?
options: A ticket to go and come back
A ticket for one direction only
A ticket you can use any day
items.correct: A ticket to go and come back
items.explanation: Round-trip (UK: return) es ida y vuelta.

items.question: What does <all-inclusive> mean for a hotel?
options: Meals and drinks are included in the price
items.correct: Meals and drinks are included in the price
items.explanation: All-inclusive incluye comidas y bebidas en el precio.

items.question: What is <backpacking>?
items.explanation: Backpacking es viajar barato con mochila.

items.question: What does <break the ice> mean?
options: To start a conversation in an awkward situation
items.correct: To start a conversation in an awkward situation
items.explanation: Break the ice: romper la tensión inicial.

items.question: What does <cost an arm and a leg> mean?
items.explanation: Cost an arm and a leg: costar un ojo de la cara.

items.question: If something is <a blessing in disguise>, it:
options: seems bad at first but turns out to be good
items.correct: seems bad at first but turns out to be good
items.explanation: Blessing in disguise: no hay mal que por bien no venga.

items.question: What does <hit the books> mean?
items.explanation: Hit the books: ponerse a estudiar en serio.

items.question: Which phrasal verb means "to arrive" (a train, a plane)?
items.explanation: Get in: llegar. Get over: superar. Get by: apañárselas.

items.question: Complete: 'I need to ___ this form before the interview.'
items.explanation: Fill in (o fill out) a form: rellenar un formulario.

items.question: Escucha y elige la frase que oíste.
items.explanation: Distinguir <doesn't/didn't> y <live/leave> de oído es lo que se está midiendo.

items.question: Escucha la pregunta y elige la mejor respuesta.
items.audioText: Would you like something to drink?
options: Yes, please — a glass of water.
items.correct: Yes, please — a glass of water.
items.explanation: <Would you like...?> es un ofrecimiento; se responde aceptando o declinando.

items.question: Escucha y responde: ¿a qué hora sale el tren?
items.audioText: The train leaves at a quarter to nine.
items.explanation: <A quarter to nine> son las nueve menos cuarto: 8:45.

items.question: Complete: 'If you can't sleep, try ___ some warm milk.'
items.explanation: <Try + -ing> = probar algo a ver si funciona; <try to> = esforzarse.

items.question: Which verb changes meaning depending on whether it's followed by gerund or infinitive?
items.explanation: Remember doing = recordar algo hecho; remember to do = acordarse de hacerlo.

items.question: Complete: 'I'm really looking forward to ___ you next week.'
items.explanation: <Look forward to> lleva <to> preposición, así que va gerundio.

items.question: Escribe UNA palabra: 'I regret ___ you that the post has been filled.' (formal, en -ing)
items.explanation: <Regret + -ing> en registro formal introduce una mala noticia.

items.question: Complete: 'If I ___ more money, I would travel around the world.'
items.explanation: Segundo condicional (situación irreal en presente): If + pasado, would.

items.question: Complete: 'If she had left earlier, she ___ the train.'
items.explanation: Tercer condicional: If + past perfect, would have + participio.

items.question: Escribe UNA palabra: 'Take an umbrella ___ case it rains.'
items.explanation: <In case> introduce una precaución ante algo que podría pasar.

items.question: Complete: 'English ___ in over 60 countries.'
items.explanation: Pasiva de presente simple: is/are + participio.

items.question: Complete: 'The bridge ___ when we arrived.'
items.explanation: Pasiva en past continuous: was/were being + participio.

items.question: Complete: 'She isn't answering her phone. She ___ be asleep.'
items.explanation: <Must> expresa deducción lógica sobre el presente.

items.question: Complete: 'He ___ have finished already — he only started an hour ago.'
items.explanation: La deducción negativa usa <can't have>, no <mustn't have>.

items.question: Complete: 'The woman ___ lives next door is a doctor.'
items.explanation: <Who> es el relativo para personas en función de sujeto.

items.question: Complete: 'That's the writer ___ novel won the prize.'
items.explanation: <Whose> marca posesión: la novela del escritor.

items.question: Escribe UNA palabra: 'Paris, ___ I visited last year, is beautiful.'
items.explanation: En relativas explicativas (con comas) no se puede usar <that>.

items.question: "Are you coming?" she asked. → She asked ___ I was coming.
items.explanation: Las preguntas de sí/no en indirecto se introducen con if/whether.

items.question: "Where do you live?" → He asked me where ___.
items.explanation: En la pregunta indirecta el orden vuelve a sujeto + verbo, sin auxiliar.

items.question: Complete: 'I need to have my car ___ tomorrow.'
items.explanation: Causativo: have + objeto + participio (lo hace otro por ti).

items.question: Complete: 'They ___ their house painted last summer.'
items.explanation: <Get something done> es la variante coloquial de <have something done>.

items.question: Complete: 'I wish I ___ how to drive.'
items.explanation: Wish + pasado simple expresa un deseo irreal en presente.

items.question: Complete: 'You ___ so fast — you got a ticket.'
items.explanation: <Shouldn't have> + participio critica algo ya ocurrido.

items.question: Escribe UNA palabra: 'If ___ I had listened to your advice!'
items.explanation: <If only> intensifica el arrepentimiento, más que <I wish>.

items.question: Complete: '___ the rain, we went for a walk.
items.explanation: <Despite/in spite of> van con sustantivo; <although> con oración.

items.question: Complete: 'He studied hard; ___, he failed the exam.'
items.explanation: <However> conecta dos oraciones independientes con contraste.

items.question: Escribe UNA palabra: 'She left early ___ that she could catch the train.' (finalidad)
items.explanation: <So that> + oración introduce la finalidad.

items.question: Which phrasal verb means "to delay or postpone"?
items.explanation: Put off: aplazar. Put up with: soportar. Put out: apagar.

items.question: Which phrasal verb means "to stop doing something, often a habit"?
items.explanation: Give up: dejar (un hábito). Give in: ceder.

items.question: What does <run out of> mean?
options: To have no more of something
items.correct: To have no more of something
items.explanation: Run out of: quedarse sin algo.

items.question: What does <back to square one> mean?
items.explanation: Back to square one: volver a empezar de cero.

items.question: If someone feels <under the weather>, they:
items.explanation: Under the weather: sentirse pachucho.

items.question: What does <let the cat out of the bag> mean?
options: To reveal a secret by accident
items.correct: To reveal a secret by accident
items.explanation: Let the cat out of the bag: irse de la lengua.

items.question: If you <procrastinate>, you:
options: keep postponing what you should do
items.correct: keep postponing what you should do
items.explanation: Procrastinate: dejar las cosas para después.

items.question: A <reliable> colleague is one who:
options: can be trusted to do what they promise
is easy to get along with
items.correct: can be trusted to do what they promise
items.explanation: Reliable: fiable, de quien te puedes fiar.

items.question: Escucha y elige qué ocurrió en realidad.
items.audioText: If I'd known, I would have told you.
options: The speaker did not know, and did not tell.
The speaker knew, but said nothing.
The speaker will tell you later.
The speaker is not sure whether they knew.
items.correct: The speaker did not know, and did not tell.
items.explanation: El tercer condicional describe algo contrario a los hechos: no lo supo, así que no lo dijo.

items.question: Escucha y elige la frase que oíste.
items.audioText: He said he'd been waiting for over an hour.
options: He said he'd been waiting for over an hour.
He said he'd waited for over an hour.
He says he's been waiting for over an hour.
He said he'd be waiting for over an hour.
items.correct: He said he'd been waiting for over an hour.
items.explanation: Hay que oír el past perfect continuo (he'd been waiting) frente a las otras tres formas.

items.question: Escucha y elige qué quiere decir quien habla.
items.audioText: I'm afraid that's out of the question.
items.explanation: <Out of the question> es un rechazo tajante, no una duda.

items.question: Not only ___ the exam, but he also got the highest score.
items.explanation: Tras <Not only> al inicio hay inversión sujeto-auxiliar.

items.question: Never before ___ such a beautiful sunset.
items.explanation: <Never before> en posición inicial exige inversión.

items.question: ___ had she sat down when the phone rang.
items.explanation: <Hardly ... when> describe dos hechos casi simultáneos.

items.question: Complete: '___ was John who broke the vase, not his sister.'
items.explanation: Oración escindida (cleft) enfática: It was X who/that...

items.question: Which sentence emphasises the action itself?
options: What he did was resign on the spot
It was on the spot that he resigned
items.correct: What he did was resign on the spot
items.explanation: La cleft con <What...> enfatiza la acción, no el sujeto ni el lugar.

items.question: Escribe UNA palabra: '___ we need is a clear deadline.' (cleft enfática)
items.explanation: La pseudo-cleft empieza con <What> + oración + be.

items.question: Complete: 'If she had studied medicine, she ___ a doctor now.'
items.explanation: Condicional mixta: causa pasada (had studied) → efecto presente (would be).

items.question: Which advanced conditional is correct?
options: Had I known, I would have helped
If I would have known, I would have helped
If I knew, I would have helped yesterday
Had I know, I would help
items.correct: Had I known, I would have helped
items.explanation: Condicional invertida: <Had> + sujeto + participio, sin <if>.

items.question: Escribe UNA palabra: '___ it not been for your help, we would have failed.'
items.explanation: Inversión de <If it had not been for>: Had it not been for...

items.question: Complete: 'It's high time you ___ your homework.'
items.explanation: <It's high time> va con pasado simple aunque hable del presente.

items.question: Complete: 'I'd rather you ___ tell anyone about this.'
items.explanation: <I'd rather + sujeto> exige pasado simple para hablar del presente.

items.question: Complete: '___ in 1890, the theatre is the oldest in the city.'
items.explanation: La cláusula de participio pasivo reduce <which was built>.

items.question: Complete: '___ finished the report, she went home.'
items.explanation: <Having + participio> marca una acción anterior a la principal.

items.question: Escribe UNA palabra: '___ by the noise, he couldn't concentrate.' (participio de distract)
items.explanation: El participio pasado en cabeza equivale a <Because he was distracted>.

items.question: Which phrasal verb means "to include something in a calculation or plan"?
items.explanation: Factor in: tener algo en cuenta al calcular o planificar.

items.question: Which phrasal verb means "to finally find time to do something after a delay"?
items.explanation: Get round to (US: get around to): sacar por fin tiempo para algo.

items.question: Which phrasal verb means "to reduce gradually"?
items.explanation: Scale back: recortar o reducir progresivamente.

items.question: If someone <barks up the wrong tree>, they:
options: are pursuing a mistaken course of action
items.correct: are pursuing a mistaken course of action
items.explanation: Bark up the wrong tree: ir por el camino equivocado.

items.question: If a company <cuts corners>, it:
options: does something cheaply, ignoring rules or quality
items.correct: does something cheaply, ignoring rules or quality
items.explanation: Cut corners: hacer las cosas a medias para ahorrar.

items.question: If a plan is <on the back burner>, it is:
items.explanation: On the back burner: aparcado, en segundo plano.

items.question: Which word collocates with <make>?
items.explanation: <Make a decision> es la colocación estándar; con research va <do>.

items.question: Complete: 'The report ___ serious concerns about safety.'
items.explanation: <Raise concerns> es la colocación fija; <rise> es intransitivo.

items.question: Complete: 'She ___ a heavy price for that decision.'
items.explanation: <Pay a heavy price> es la colocación establecida.

items.question: Which sentence hedges the claim most cautiously?
options: The data suggest a possible link
The data show the link clearly
items.correct: The data suggest a possible link
items.explanation: <Suggest> + <possible> atenúa la afirmación, propio del registro académico.

items.question: Complete (academic register): 'The results ___ that the treatment is effective.'
items.explanation: La escritura académica prefiere fórmulas atenuadas y evita lo tajante.

items.question: Complete: 'The minister ___ to have misled parliament.'
items.explanation: Pasiva de reporte: <It is alleged that...> → <He is alleged to have...>.

items.question: Complete: 'The scheme ___ to be costing far more than expected.'
items.explanation: Misma estructura de pasiva impersonal con verbos de opinión.

items.question: Escribe UNA palabra: 'The building is said ___ have been designed by Gaudí.'
items.explanation: Pasiva de reporte con infinitivo perfecto: is said to have been...

items.question: Complete: '___, the proposal is sound; in practice, it is unworkable.'
items.explanation: <In principle ... in practice> es el par contrastivo esperado.

items.question: Complete: 'The budget was cut; ___, three projects were cancelled.'
items.explanation: <Consequently> marca consecuencia, no contraste ni simultaneidad.

items.question: Escucha y elige qué opina quien habla de esa fuente.
items.audioText: She's hardly the most reliable source.
options: The speaker considers the source unreliable.
The speaker trusts the source completely.
The speaker has not read the source.
The speaker thinks the source is the best available.
items.correct: The speaker considers the source unreliable.
items.explanation: <Hardly> niega con ironía: no es precisamente la fuente más fiable.

items.question: Escucha y elige qué es cierto según lo que oíste.
items.audioText: Not only was the report late, it was also incomplete.
options: The report had two separate problems.
The report was late but otherwise fine.
The report was complete but early.
The report was neither late nor incomplete.
items.correct: The report had two separate problems.
items.explanation: <Not only... but also> suma dos defectos; la inversión marca el énfasis.

items.question: Escucha y elige qué quiere decir quien habla.
items.audioText: I'd sooner not comment at this stage.
options: They prefer not to say anything for now.
They have no opinion on the matter.
They were told not to comment.
items.correct: They prefer not to say anything for now.
items.explanation: <I'd sooner not> expresa preferencia por abstenerse, no una prohibición.

items.question: Which sentence correctly uses <scarcely ... when> to express immediacy?
options: Scarcely had we arrived when the storm broke
Scarcely we had arrived when the storm broke
Scarcely we arrived than the storm broke
Scarcely had we arrived than the storm broke
items.correct: Scarcely had we arrived when the storm broke
items.explanation: <Scarcely> exige inversión y se empareja con <when>, no con <than>.

items.question: Complete: 'Under no circumstances ___ the door be left unlocked.'
items.explanation: Tras una expresión negativa en cabeza se invierte auxiliar y sujeto.

items.question: Complete: 'So compelling ___ her argument that nobody objected.'
items.explanation: <So + adjetivo> en cabeza fuerza inversión: So compelling was her argument...

items.question: Choose the correct use of the mandative subjunctive in formal writing:
options: The board insists that he resign immediately
The board insists that he resigns immediately
The board insists that he will resign immediately
The board insists him to resign immediately
items.correct: The board insists that he resign immediately
items.explanation: El subjuntivo mandativo usa la forma base del verbo, sin -s.

items.question: Complete: 'It is essential that every application ___ by Friday.'
items.explanation: Tras <it is essential that> el verbo va en subjuntivo: be submitted.

items.question: Escribe UNA palabra: 'We recommend that the policy ___ reviewed annually.' (subjuntivo)
items.explanation: El subjuntivo mandativo mantiene <be> invariable tras <recommend that>.

items.question: When is <albeit> used?
options: To introduce a concession, usually before an adjective or phrase
items.correct: To introduce a concession, usually before an adjective or phrase
items.explanation: <Albeit> = although it is: a modest, albeit welcome, improvement.

items.question: Complete: '___ the evidence is thin, the conclusion remains plausible.'
items.explanation: <Granted that> concede el punto; las otras introducen causa.

items.question: Complete: 'Much ___ I admire her work, I cannot support this proposal.'
items.explanation: <Much as> + oración es la estructura concesiva enfática.

items.question: What does <a moot point> mean?
options: An issue that is debatable or no longer relevant
items.correct: An issue that is debatable or no longer relevant
items.explanation: Moot point: cuestión discutible o ya irrelevante.

items.question: If a claim <does not hold water>, it:
items.explanation: Hold water: sostenerse ante el examen crítico.

items.question: If someone <damns something with faint praise>, they:
options: criticise it by praising it only mildly
items.correct: criticise it by praising it only mildly
items.explanation: Damn with faint praise: criticar mediante un elogio tibio.

items.question: Which is the most formal way to introduce a limitation?
options: It should be noted, however, that the sample was small
But the sample was pretty small
items.correct: It should be noted, however, that the sample was small
items.explanation: El registro formal prefiere la pasiva impersonal y evita coloquialismos.

items.question: Which verb is most appropriate in academic prose?
items.explanation: <Ascertain> es el equivalente formal de <find out>.

items.question: If a researcher <delves into> a topic, they:
items.explanation: Delve into: profundizar, escarbar en un tema.

items.question: Complete: 'The findings ___ serious doubt on the earlier study.'
items.explanation: <Cast doubt on> es la colocación fija.

items.question: Complete: 'The two accounts are difficult to ___.'
items.explanation: <Reconcile accounts/versions>: hacerlas compatibles entre sí.

items.question: Complete: 'The policy is costly; ___, it is the only viable option.'
items.explanation: <That said> introduce una concesión tras una crítica.

items.question: Complete: 'The rule applies ___ the parties have agreed otherwise.'
items.explanation: <Unless and until> es la fórmula fija del registro jurídico-formal.

items.question: Escribe UNA palabra: 'The scheme was, ___ large, a success.' (= en general)
items.explanation: <By and large> significa <en términos generales>.

items.question: Escucha y elige qué le pasó a la propuesta.
items.audioText: The proposal was, by all accounts, dead in the water.
options: It had no chance of succeeding.
It was revived after a delay.
items.correct: It had no chance of succeeding.
items.explanation: <Dead in the water>: sin ninguna posibilidad de prosperar.

items.question: Escucha y elige qué está haciendo quien habla.
items.audioText: Far be it from me to question her judgement.
options: Ironically signalling that they do question it
items.correct: Ironically signalling that they do question it
items.explanation: <Far be it from me to...> introduce casi siempre la crítica que dice no querer hacer.
